Pick the cheapest specialist whose agent description fits and whose result you can judge. The route table, not the brief, sets model and effort, so a brief never names either; the specialist's `holyagent:<agent>` name is the `agentType` of its workflow `agent()`. Haiku routes take mechanical and read-only work: Worker.mechanical for data, list or count corrections and for resolving conflicts in tests or generated files, Worker.validation for gate runs, Worker.operations for builds and screenshot capture, and the lookup and map roles for finding facts. Sonnet routes take work that needs judgment: implementation, integration, debugging, visual work and the code, testing and security reviews. A bug with a known reproduction goes to Worker.implementation (fix and regression test); Worker.debugging takes unknown causes. With several Intents open and none in use, choose one through AskUserQuestion.
